incidents.victim: ASOS (British online fashion retailer)
incidents.vector: Attackers obtained a single stolen employee credential to access ASOS systems and compromise the company's Snowflake cloud data environment.
incidents.impact: Approximately 17 million customer records stolen including names, addresses, phone numbers, email, date of birth, and purchase history; attackers sent push notifications to all ASOS app users; stock fell 13%.

incidents.victim: Global critical infrastructure, government, healthcare, and IT organizations
incidents.attacker: China — state-linked espionage group (Integrity Technology Group)
incidents.vector: Actors combined automated vulnerability scanning, large-scale botnets, cross-site scripting payloads, and password spraying against Microsoft Exchange to gain initial access, then established persistence via SoftEther VPN and exfiltrated credentials and email data.
incidents.impact: Nine-nation joint advisory AA26-281A issued Oct 8 by FBI, CISA, NSA, UK NCSC, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain; victims confirmed across government, critical manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, and education in North America, Southeast Asia, and Africa.

incidents.victim: Multiple South Korean financial institutions
incidents.vector: Attacker used the ARTEX open-source pentesting framework augmented with large language models to automate attack steps, exploiting web application vulnerabilities across multiple South Korean banks.
incidents.impact: Multiple banks breached with data exfiltrated; CrowdStrike forensics recovered attacker's AI chat history, revealing a low-skill operator using Claude to compensate for limited technical capability; campaign active late September through early October 2026.

incidents.victim: Iraqi telecom, aviation, and critical infrastructure organizations
incidents.vector: Attackers posed as Dubai Airports IT staff to deliver malicious .csproj project files via fake job lures, deploying ShelbyLoader V2 malware with GitHub-based command-and-control infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Ongoing infiltration of Iraqi telecommunications, aviation, and critical infrastructure organizations; campaign active since November 2025, most recently observed in March 2026; Palo Alto Unit 42 published IOCs and TTP details.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate firewall and VPN users globally
incidents.vector: Attackers harvested and GPU-cracked credentials from internet-exposed Fortinet FortiGate SSL VPN appliances, using credential stuffing from prior leak dumps and infostealer logs; cracked access packaged and sold to ransomware affiliates.
incidents.impact: Over 86,644 devices confirmed compromised across 194 countries; some victims locked out of their own firewalls after attackers deleted or changed credentials; serves as initial access pipeline for INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware groups; FBI/USSS joint advisory issued October 6.

incidents.victim: US banks and ATM networks
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ATM jackpotting (Tren de Aragua)
incidents.vector: Venezuelan criminal organization deployed ATM jackpotting malware that forced cash dispensing from bank ATMs across the United States, operating since August 2025.
incidents.impact: $40.73 million stolen across more than 1,500 attacks; US Treasury OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and entities in Operation Economic Outcast; campaign remains active.

incidents.victim: US Department of Defense — Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC)
incidents.vector: A misconfigured file-sharing system was left publicly accessible from October 2025 through July 2026, during which unauthorized parties accessed sensitive military personnel records.
incidents.impact: 3.1 million records exposed including 2.8 million living military personnel and 294,000 deceased; data includes names, Social Security numbers, and military unit information; accessible for approximately nine months before discovery.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware actors deployed malware into ATNS operational technology (OT) networks providing weather services to air traffic controllers; insider collaboration is under investigation.
incidents.impact: Attack targeted systems that manage 6% of the world's airspace and could have disrupted both domestic and international air travel; ATNS investigating possible employee involvement with the attackers.

incidents.victim: Organizations globally running Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited three zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772, CVE-2026-88779) in Citrix NetScaler appliances; exploitation of CVE-2026-88772 began September 3 and ran undetected for over three weeks before patches were available.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations confirmed compromised across North America and Europe spanning government, financial services, education, telecom, and legal sectors; 50,000+ publicly exposed instances potentially vulnerable; Mandiant attributes attacks to advanced suspected state-sponsored actors.

incidents.victim: Bitget cryptocurrency exchange (Singapore)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one of three hot wallet layers maintained by the exchange, draining customer-facing liquidity pools.
incidents.impact: Over $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from Bitget hot wallets; the largest single crypto theft of 2026.

incidents.victim: FBI recruitment portal (FBIjobs.gov)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 via an unpatched Accenture contractor environment, defacing FBIjobs.gov and exfiltrating FBI personnel records; exploitation of the vulnerability had been ongoing since June 2026.
incidents.impact: Over 5,000 FBI agent records exposed including medical records, home addresses, phone numbers, unit assignments, and task force details; three arrests made in October 2026 in the Netherlands, Jordan, and Pennsylvania; same criminal group extorted $70M+ across a broader 2026 campaign.

incidents.victim: Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing aviation subsidiary)
incidents.vector: Criminal group leveraged data stolen through mass Oracle PeopleSoft exploitation to extort ForeFlight, a Boeing aviation spin-off sold to Thoma Bravo in November 2025 for $10.55 billion.
incidents.impact: Aviation software provider serving commercial and military pilots targeted for extortion; scope of stolen data not publicly confirmed; part of a broader campaign that extorted $70M+ across multiple victims in 2026.

incidents.victim: Taiwan research organizations and Asian government and policy agencies
incidents.vector: Two separate China-nexus threat groups used spear-phishing campaigns: one deployed the Antino backdoor against government and policy organizations across Asia; the second targeted Taiwanese research institutions using tailored lure documents.
incidents.impact: Multiple government and research organizations across Asia-Pacific infiltrated in ongoing intelligence collection operations; Cisco Talos and CyberScoop published indicators and TTP analysis.

incidents.victim: DIVD (Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure)
incidents.vector: An AI-driven attack agent breached the internal systems of DIVD, a Dutch cybersecurity non-profit that coordinates vulnerability disclosures between researchers and software vendors.
incidents.impact: DIVD internal systems compromised; investigation ongoing at time of reporting; one of the first publicly confirmed AI-agent-driven breaches of a cybersecurity organization.

incidents.victim: Danish government Central Person Register (CPR)
incidents.vector: Unknown attackers breached the Danish government's national identity registry database in September 2026, exfiltrating records before the intrusion was detected on October 2.
incidents.impact: 8 million Danish citizens' records stolen, effectively the entire registered population of Denmark; one of the largest government database breaches in European history.

incidents.victim: Spanish and Portuguese water utility, telecom, regional government, and university
incidents.vector: Warlock ransomware group conducted coordinated attacks against multiple organizations in Spain and Portugal, encrypting systems and exfiltrating data in a double-extortion scheme.
incidents.impact: Four organizations across critical infrastructure and public sector impacted; operational disruptions reported; Cisco Talos published Warlock ransomware technical analysis.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (Axios npm, Mastra AI packages, Rust arrayref crate)
incidents.vector: North Korea-affiliated actors injected malicious code into the widely used Axios npm package (adding plain-crypto-js), Mastra AI packages, and the Rust arrayref crate to steal cloud authentication tokens and code-signing certificates from developer environments.
incidents.impact: Potentially thousands of developer pipelines exposed; cloud credentials and code-signing certificates targeted for subsequent infrastructure access or software tampering; Palo Alto Unit 42 published full technical analysis.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Ransomware group breached ATF systems, encrypting data and exfiltrating sensitive law enforcement case files and investigative records.
incidents.impact: ATF confirmed ransomware compromise; attackers leaked information about active ATF investigative targets; the same group was the second most active ransomware operator globally in July 2026 with 127 attacks.

incidents.victim: iRhythm Technologies (cardiac biosensor company)
incidents.vector: Attackers used social engineering to access iRhythm's third-party-hosted business applications between June 3 and June 8, downloading patient records; a ransom demand was subsequently sent to the company.
incidents.impact: At least 368,173 patients affected across multiple US states; stolen data includes names, addresses, iRhythm device serial numbers, insurance numbers, dates of birth, and cardiac monitoring service dates; disclosed via state breach filings in October 2026.

incidents.victim: Fideuram (Intesa Sanpaolo private banking arm), Italy
incidents.vector: Fraudsters used AI-generated voice cloning to impersonate Intesa Sanpaolo CEO Carlo Messina and an attorney, convincing Fideuram's chairman to approve wire transfers to Chinese and Hong Kong bank accounts.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108 million) fraudulently transferred; Intesa recovered more than half the funds but €36 million remains unrecovered; one of the largest confirmed AI-assisted financial frauds on record.
